established_findings.statement: Large language models can translate natural-language intents into network-configuration artifacts in controlled demonstrations, typically using fine-tuning or in-context examples.
limitations: Published demonstrations are mostly small- to medium-scale and use constrained task formats (JSON templates, NFV use cases).
Generality across diverse topologies, vendors, and real production policies is not established in these records.

established_findings.statement: LLM-alone generation is brittle: models frequently produce syntax, semantic, or topology errors; interposing deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish) and iterative repair substantially improves correctness in reported studies.
limitations: Improvements reported are from prototype workflows and case studies rather than broad production deployments.
The verifier+repair loops still often require human oversight or human-defined specifications to be effective.

established_findings.statement: Constraint-based adaptation and verifier-augmented validator designs enable higher accuracy and safer abstention behaviour for LLM-assisted NetOps tasks in evaluated settings.
limitations: Reported accuracy gains are task- and dataset-dependent; results do not yet demonstrate end-to-end deployment at Internet scale.
Some failure modes (types of misconfigurations) remain hard for these systems to detect.

established_findings.statement: Agentic/tool-enabled LLM workflows introduce exploitable excessive-agency and tool-selection risks; secure-by-default guardrails and human-approval gates are proposed as necessary mitigations.
limitations: Mitigation proposals are engineering/archival; their effectiveness in diverse NetOps deployments remains to be empirically validated.
Attack surfaces vary with tool integrations and provider APIs; specific risk profiles depend on implementation details.

unresolved_questions.statement: How well do closed-loop generate–verify–repair (GVR) workflows scale and generalize across multi-vendor, multi-router, and large-topology operator networks?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: Current demonstrations and prototypes show feasibility but limited-scale evaluation
limitations: Existing papers report gains on constrained tasks or single-case studies; none provide comprehensive large-scale, multi-vendor generalization experiments within the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do LLM-assisted NetOps workflows yield measurable operational benefits (reachability/policy compliance, MTTR reduction, outage risk) when integrated end-to-end with emulators/verifiers and operator processes?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: Related pipeline and benchmark proposals (partial/adjacent evidence)
limitations: UniAIOps and SREGym provide related evaluation infrastructure or SRE benchmarks but do not establish generalized, quantified production NetOps outcomes for intent-to-config pipelines in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: How robust are agentic NetOps systems to adversarial prompt/tool-context injection and to hallucination propagation when given tool access?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: Empirical audits and engineering threat analyses
limitations: Audits demonstrate high-risk vectors and guardrail approaches, but the security posture of concrete NetOps toolchains under adaptive adversaries is not fully characterized in these records.

candidate_gaps.statement: A public, standardized benchmark that couples intent-to-configuration tasks with formal verification (e.g., Batfish), emulator execution, and operator-meaningful metrics is lacking in the supplied literature.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: Survey of existing benchmarks and task papers showing adjacent but incomplete coverage
limitations: SREGym and UniAIOps exist for SRE/AIOps evaluation, and PreConfig/intent papers provide tasks, but none of the supplied records present a widely adopted, verifier-coupled NetOps benchmark with execution/emulation and standard metrics.

candidate_gaps.statement: Systematic studies of repair-loop budgeting, stopping rules, and statistical guarantees for iterative LLM repair in NetOps are insufficiently developed in the supplied records.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: Architectural proposals and iterative-debugging studies in related domains
limitations: GVR and iterative debugging architectures are proposed and studied mainly in software/code contexts or single-case enterprise settings; explicit, quantitatively principled stopping-rule evaluations for networking tasks are not evident in the supplied materials.

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirical evaluations comparing verifier-feedback strategies (localized actionable feedback vs. global failure signals) for efficient LLM repair in network configuration synthesis are sparse.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: Prototype studies and verifier-tool evolution papers
limitations: The 2023 verified-prompt programming work demonstrates localized-feedback value in case studies; Batfish literature documents verification capabilities, but systematic head-to-head comparisons of feedback granularity strategies are not present in the supplied records.

excluded_claims: LLMs are proven production-ready for fully autonomous NetOps without human oversight (unsupported by supplied records).
LLMs reliably generate correct network configurations without any external verifier or repair loop (contradicted by supplied evidence of brittleness and hallucination).
Any single LLM is universally superior across all NetOps tasks (no supplied record supports such a universal superiority claim).
The supplied literature demonstrates that hallucination risk is absent in LLM-assisted NetOps (supplied records report hallucinations and hallucinated fixes).
